synthesis.body: When bash invokes a Python heredoc as `python3 - args <<PY ... PY` and the heredoc ends with `sys.exit(1 if violations else 0)`, the heredoc's rc is captured by `$?` as exactly 0 or 1 — bash callers everywhere pattern-match on `rc -eq 1`. A naive port that hoists the heredoc body into a Python function returning `violations` (an int count) and `sys.exit(<count>)` at the top level silently widens the rc shape: with 2+ violations, rc=2; rc>125 is reserved territory. Callers like `tools/test-*.sh`'s `[[ $got -eq 1 ]]` or a CI `if rc == 1` branch silently miss the failure. Aggregators that only check non-zero (like our `pre-pr.py`) mask this further. The fix is one line: `return 1 if violations else 0` at every exit site. Bit us in the post-EXECUTE review of windows-hooks-phase3; lint-build.py's two return paths both leaked the count. Generalises to any bash-heredoc-to-Python-function port — the parity-pinning bar is the rc *shape*, not just "non-zero on failure".

title: Bash-to-Python port: heredoc rc was normalised; naked `return violations` leaks the raw count
